```java
package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
    }

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.GREEN);
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        var in = new Scanner(System.in);
        Move move;
        while (true) {
            System.out.printf("[%s] Make a Move: ", game.getCurrentPlayer().getName());
            var moveStr = in.nextLine().toLowerCase();
            move = parseMove(moveStr);
            if (move != null) {
                var error = validateMove(game, move);
                if (error != null) {
                    System.out.println("[Invalid Move]: " + error);
                    continue;
                }
                break;
            }
            System.out.println("[Invalid Move]: Incorrect format");
        }
        return move;
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[]{
                new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
                new OccupiedRule(),
                new VacantRule(),
                new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
                new ArcherMoveRule(),
                new KnightMoveRule(),
                new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule :
                rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }

            var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
            if (piece == null) {
                return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
            }
            if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
                return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
            var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        var segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
```
```java
    }
```
}

I'll help complete the `validate` method for the `KnightBlockRule` class. Based on the Wikipedia link about Xiangqi (Chinese chess) horses, a knight/horse can be blocked if there's a piece in the adjacent square between its current position and destination.

Here's the completed method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    int dx = Math.abs(dest.x() - source.x());
    int dy = Math.abs(dest.y() - source.y());
    
    // Knight moves in L-shape (1x2 or 2x1)
    if (!((dx == 1 && dy == 2) || (dx == 2 && dy == 1))) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Check for blocking piece (horse's leg)
    int blockX = source.x() + (dest.x() - source.x()) / 2;
    int blockY = source.y() + (dest.y() - source.y()) / 2;
    Place blockPlace = new Place(blockX, blockY);
    
    return game.getPiece(blockPlace) == null;
}
```

Explanation:
1. First checks if the moving piece is a Knight (already implemented)
2. Calculates the x and y differences between source and destination
3. Verifies it's a valid L-shaped knight move (1x2 or 2x1)
4. Calculates the blocking position (the adjacent square between source and destination)
5. Returns true only if there's no piece in the blocking position

This implements the Chinese chess horse blocking rule where a knight cannot jump over an adjacent piece. The blocking position is calculated as the midpoint between source and destination (rounded towards source since we're dealing with integer coordinates).

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");
        }
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Total Moves: " + this.numMoves);
        // print scores of players
        for (var player :
                this.configuration.getPlayers()) {
            System.out.printf("%s%s%s score: %d\n", player.getColor(), player.getName(), Color.DEFAULT,
                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        for (int row = contents.size() - 1; row >= 0; row--) {

    }

    }

        return this.getPiece(new Place(x, y));
    }

    }
```

```java
/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

}
```

Based on the task description and the provided code context, I'll complete the `validate` method in the `ArcherMoveRule` class. The Archer's movement is similar to the cannon in Chinese chess (Xiangqi), which moves like a rook (orthogonally any distance) but must jump over exactly one piece to capture.

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }
    
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    
    // Check if moving orthogonally (same row or same column)
    if (source.x() != dest.x() && source.y() != dest.y()) {
        return false;
    }
    
    int dx = Integer.compare(dest.x(), source.x());
    int dy = Integer.compare(dest.y(), source.y());
    int piecesBetween = 0;
    
    // Count pieces between source and destination
    Place current = new Place(source.x() + dx, source.y() + dy);
    while (!current.equals(dest)) {
        if (game.getPiece(current) != null) {
            piecesBetween++;
        }
        current = new Place(current.x() + dx, current.y() + dy);
    }
    
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(dest);
    if (destPiece == null) {
        // Moving to empty square - must have no pieces between
        return piecesBetween == 0;
    } else {
        // Capturing - must have exactly one piece between
        return piecesBetween == 1;
    }
}
```

Explanation:
1. First checks if the piece being moved is an Archer (already implemented)
2. Verifies the move is orthogonal (same row or column)
3. Counts pieces between source and destination
4. For empty destination: requires no pieces between (like rook)
5. For occupied destination (capture): requires exactly one piece between (like cannon)
6. Returns true if the move is valid according to Archer rules, false otherwise

This implementation follows the cannon movement rules from Chinese chess where:
- Normal moves (no capture) are like a rook (no jumping)
- Captures require jumping exactly one piece

```java
/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");
        }
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Total Moves: " + this.numMoves);
        // print scores of players
        for (var player :
                this.configuration.getPlayers()) {
            System.out.printf("%s%s%s score: %d\n", player.getColor(), player.getName(), Color.DEFAULT,
                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        for (int row = contents.size() - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            System.out.printf("%" + (leftPadding - 1) + "d|%s|%d\n",

        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",

        System.out.println();
```

The error occurs because the `Place` and `Piece` classes need to be imported. Here's the corrected method with the necessary imports:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }
    
    assignment.protocol.Place source = move.getSource();
    assignment.protocol.Place dest = move.getDestination();
    
    // Check if moving orthogonally (same row or same column)
    if (source.x() != dest.x() && source.y() != dest.y()) {
        return false;
    }
    
    int dx = Integer.compare(dest.x(), source.x());
    int dy = Integer.compare(dest.y(), source.y());
    int piecesBetween = 0;
    
    // Count pieces between source and destination
    assignment.protocol.Place current = new assignment.protocol.Place(source.x() + dx, source.y() + dy);
    while (!current.equals(dest)) {
        if (game.getPiece(current) != null) {
            piecesBetween++;
        }
        current = new assignment.protocol.Place(current.x() + dx, current.y() + dy);
    }
    
    assignment.protocol.Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(dest);
    if (destPiece == null) {
        // Moving to empty square - must have no pieces between
        return piecesBetween == 0;
    } else {
        // Capturing - must have exactly one piece between
        return piecesBetween == 1;
    }
}
```

I'll help complete the `validate` method for the `FirstNMovesProtectionRule` class. This rule prevents piece capturing during the first N moves of the game.

The method should:
1. Check if the current move number is within the protected range
2. If it is, verify that the move doesn't capture any piece
3. Return true if the move is valid according to this rule

Here's the complete method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    // If we're past the protected moves, the rule doesn't apply
    if (game.getNumMoves() >= numProtectedMoves) {
        return true;
    }
    
    // Check if the destination has an opponent's piece (would be a capture)
    Piece destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    if (destinationPiece != null) {
        // Check if it's an opponent's piece (not same player)
        Piece sourcePiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (sourcePiece != null && !sourcePiece.getPlayer().equals(destinationPiece.getPlayer())) {
            return false; // Capturing opponent's piece during protected moves
        }
    }
    
    return true;
}
```

Explanation:
1. First checks if we're still within the protected move count (numProtectedMoves)
2. If we are, checks if the move would capture an opponent's piece
3. Returns false if there's an attempted capture during protected moves
4. Otherwise returns true (move is valid according to this rule)

The method follows the rule's purpose of preventing piece captures during the initial phase of the game while allowing all moves after that period.

```java
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**

public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");
        }
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Total Moves: " + this.numMoves);
        // print scores of players
        for (var player :
                this.configuration.getPlayers()) {
            System.out.printf("%s%s%s score: %d\n", player.getColor(), player.getName(), Color.DEFAULT,
                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        for (int row = contents.size() - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            System.out.printf("%" + (leftPadding - 1) + "d|%s|%d\n",
                    row + 1,
                    contents.get(row).parallelStream().map(Object::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(" ")),

        }
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        System.out.println();
    }

    /**
     * Get the piece in the place
     *
     * @param place the place of the piece
     * @return the piece
     */
    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(@NotNull Place place) {
        return this.board[place.x()][place.y()];
    }

    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(int x, int y) {
        return this.getPiece(new Place(x, y));
    }

    public Player getCurrentPlayer() {
        return currentPlayer != null ? currentPlayer : this.configuration.getPlayers()[0];
    }

        return configuration.getPlayers();
    }

    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    public Configuration getConfiguration() {
        return configuration;
    }

    public Place getCentralPlace() {
        return configuration.getCentralPlace();
    }

    @Override
    public Game clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Game) super.clone();
        cloned.configuration = this.configuration.clone();
        cloned.board = this.board.clone();
        for (int i = 0; i < this.configuration.getSize(); i++) {
            cloned.board[i] = this.board[i].clone();
            // no need to deep copy pieces
            if (this.configuration.getSize() >= 0)
                System.arraycopy(this.board[i], 0, cloned.board[i], 0, this.configuration.getSize());
        }
        cloned.currentPlayer = currentPlayer == null ? null : currentPlayer.clone();
        return cloned;
    }
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.StringJoiner;

/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

    /* Object methods end */

}
```

I'll help complete the `validate` method for the `KnightMoveRule` class. This method should validate whether a knight's move follows the standard chess rules for knight movement (L-shaped: 2 squares in one direction and then 1 square perpendicular, or vice versa).

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    
    int dx = Math.abs(destination.x() - source.x());
    int dy = Math.abs(destination.y() - source.y());
    
    // Knight moves in L-shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (dx == 2 && dy == 1) || (dx == 1 && dy == 2);
}
```

2. It gets the source and destination positions from the move
3. Calculates the absolute differences in x and y coordinates (dx and dy)
4. Returns true if the move follows the knight's L-shaped movement pattern (either 2 squares in x and 1 in y, or 1 in x and 2 in y)
5. Returns false for any other movement pattern

This implementation correctly validates knight moves according to standard chess rules while maintaining the existing interface requirements.

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");

        // print scores of players

                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),

        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        System.out.println();
    }

     * Get the piece in the place
     *
     * @param place the place of the piece
     * @return the piece
     */
    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(@NotNull Place place) {
        return this.board[place.x()][place.y()];
    }

        return this.getPiece(new Place(x, y));
    }

        return configuration.getPlayers();
    }

    }

        return configuration.getCentralPlace();
    }

    @Override
    public Game clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Game) super.clone();
        cloned.configuration = this.configuration.clone();
        cloned.board = this.board.clone();
        for (int i = 0; i < this.configuration.getSize(); i++) {
            cloned.board[i] = this.board[i].clone();
            // no need to deep copy pieces
            if (this.configuration.getSize() >= 0)
                System.arraycopy(this.board[i], 0, cloned.board[i], 0, this.configuration.getSize());
        }
        cloned.currentPlayer = currentPlayer == null ? null : currentPlayer.clone();
        return cloned;
    }
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.StringJoiner;

/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

    /* Object methods end */

}
```

I'll help complete the `getAvailableMoves` method for the Knight class. The method should return all valid L-shaped moves (like in chess) that a knight can make from its current position, considering board boundaries and other game rules.

Here's the implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    
    // All possible L-shaped moves for a knight (8 possible directions)
    int[] dx = {1, 2, 2, 1, -1, -2, -2, -1};
    int[] dy = {2, 1, -1, -2, -2, -1, 1, 2};
    
    int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    
    for (int i = 0; i < dx.length; i++) {
        int newX = source.x() + dx[i];
        int newY = source.y() + dy[i];
        
        // Check if the new position is within board boundaries
        if (newX >= 0 && newX < boardSize && newY >= 0 && newY < boardSize) {
            Place destination = new Place(newX, newY);
            Move move = new Move(source, destination);
            
            // Validate the move using the game's rules
            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                validMoves.add(move);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

Explanation:
1. The method calculates all 8 possible L-shaped moves a knight can make in chess (2 squares in one direction and 1 square perpendicular).
2. For each potential move, it checks if the destination is within the board boundaries.
3. It creates a Move object for each valid destination.
4. Each move is validated using the existing `validateMove` method which checks all game rules.
5. Valid moves are collected in a list and returned as an array.

The implementation considers:
- Board boundaries (won't suggest moves that go off the board)
- Game-specific rules (through the validateMove method)
- All possible knight moves from the current position
- Returns only moves that are actually valid according to all game rules

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {

        if (newX >= 0 && newX < boardSize && newY >= 0 && newY < boardSize) {
            Place destination = new Place(newX, newY);
            Move move = new Move(source, destination);
            
            // Validate the move using the game's rules
            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                validMoves.add(move);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);

```java
	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
```

```java
public abstract class Player implements Cloneable {

     * overriding {@link Player#equals(Object)} method.
     */
    protected final String name;

    /**
     * The game score of this player.
     * Score will be updated whenever the player makes a move through {@link Game#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)}
     * and {@link Player#setScore(int)}
     */
    protected int score;

    /**
     * The color representing this player
     */
    protected final Color color;

    public Player(String name, Color color) {
        this.name = name;
        this.color = color;
    }


    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Player player = (Player) o;
        return name.equals(player.name);
    }

    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(name);
    }

        return this.name;
    }

    }

    }

    }
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");
        }
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Total Moves: " + this.numMoves);
        // print scores of players
        for (var player :
                this.configuration.getPlayers()) {
            System.out.printf("%s%s%s score: %d\n", player.getColor(), player.getName(), Color.DEFAULT,
                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        for (int row = contents.size() - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            System.out.printf("%" + (leftPadding - 1) + "d|%s|%d\n",
                    row + 1,
                    contents.get(row).parallelStream().map(Object::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(" ")),
                    row + 1);
        }
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        System.out.println();
    }

    /**
     * Get the piece in the place
     *
     * @param place the place of the piece
     * @return the piece
     */
    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(@NotNull Place place) {
        return this.board[place.x()][place.y()];
    }

    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(int x, int y) {
        return this.getPiece(new Place(x, y));
    }

    public Player getCurrentPlayer() {
        return currentPlayer != null ? currentPlayer : this.configuration.getPlayers()[0];
    }

    public Player[] getPlayers() {
        return configuration.getPlayers();
    }

    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    public Configuration getConfiguration() {
        return configuration;
    }

    public Place getCentralPlace() {
        return configuration.getCentralPlace();
    }

    @Override
    public Game clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Game) super.clone();
        cloned.configuration = this.configuration.clone();
        cloned.board = this.board.clone();
        for (int i = 0; i < this.configuration.getSize(); i++) {
            cloned.board[i] = this.board[i].clone();
            // no need to deep copy pieces
            if (this.configuration.getSize() >= 0)
                System.arraycopy(this.board[i], 0, cloned.board[i], 0, this.configuration.getSize());
        }
        cloned.currentPlayer = currentPlayer == null ? null : currentPlayer.clone();
        return cloned;
    }
}
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

    /* Object methods end */

}
```

```java
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.StringJoiner;

/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

    /* Object methods end */

}
```

@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
```java
    int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    
    // Check if source is within bounds
    boolean sourceValid = source.x() >= 0 && source.x() < boardSize && 
                         source.y() >= 0 && source.y() < boardSize;
    
    // Check if destination is within bounds
    boolean destinationValid = destination.x() >= 0 && destination.x() < boardSize && 
                              destination.y() >= 0 && destination.y() < boardSize;
    
    return sourceValid && destinationValid;
}
```

I'll help complete the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` class. Based on the Wikipedia link provided, an Archer (Cannon) moves like a Rook (horizontally or vertically any number of squares), but captures by jumping over exactly one piece (either friendly or enemy) along the path.

Here's the implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}}; // Right, Left, Up, Down
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int x = source.x() + dx;
        int y = source.y() + dy;
        int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
        
        // Check for normal moves (without capturing)
        while (x >= 0 && x < boardSize && y >= 0 && y < boardSize) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Move move = new Move(source, dest);
            if (game.getPiece(dest) == null) { // Empty square
                if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                    validMoves.add(move);
                }
                x += dx;
                y += dy;
                continue;
            }
            break; // Hit a piece, stop in this direction for normal moves
        }
        
        // Check for capture moves (must jump over exactly one piece)
        x = source.x() + dx;
        y = source.y() + dy;
        boolean foundPiece = false;
        
        while (x >= 0 && x < boardSize && y >= 0 && y < boardSize) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Piece piece = game.getPiece(dest);
            
            if (!foundPiece) {
                if (piece != null) {
                    foundPiece = true;
                }
            } else {
                if (piece != null) {
                    // Check if it's an enemy piece
                    if (!piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayer())) {
                        Move move = new Move(source, dest);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
            x += dx;
            y += dy;
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

This implementation:
1. Checks all four directions (right, left, up, down)
2. For normal moves (non-capturing), the Archer can move any number of squares until it hits another piece
3. For capturing moves, the Archer must jump over exactly one piece (any piece) and land on an enemy piece
4. Uses the existing `validateMove` method to ensure all moves follow game rules
5. Returns an array of all valid moves

The method handles both movement and capturing according to the Cannon's rules in Xiangqi. It considers board boundaries and validates each potential move using the existing validation rules.

```java
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * Player interface for the game.
 * Implementations could be computer player or human player.

public abstract class Player implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * The name of a player.
     * By default, name is a unique identifier to distinguish different players. But this can be overrided by
     * overriding {@link Player#equals(Object)} method.
     */
    protected final String name;

    /**
     * The game score of this player.
     * Score will be updated whenever the player makes a move through {@link Game#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)}
     * and {@link Player#setScore(int)}
     */
    protected int score;

    /**
     * The color representing this player
     */
    protected final Color color;

    public Player(String name, Color color) {
        this.name = name;
        this.color = color;
    }


    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Player player = (Player) o;
        return name.equals(player.name);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(name);
    }

    public final String getName() {
        return this.name;
    }

    public final int getScore() {
        return score;
    }

    public final void setScore(int score) {
        this.score = score;
    }

    public String toString() {
        return this.name;
    }

    /**
     * Get color used to represent this player.
     *
     * @return color of this player
     */
    public final Color getColor() {
        return this.color;
    }

    @Override
    public Player clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        return (Player) super.clone();
    }

     * @param game           the current game object

    public abstract @NotNull Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves);
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

    /**
     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

    /**
     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */
    protected int numMoves = 0;

    public Game(Configuration configuration) {
        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the piece and corresponding move made by him just now.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    /**
     * Make a move.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    public abstract void movePiece(@NotNull Move move);

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

    /**
     * Refresh the output printed in the console, which shows the following things.
     * 1. the gameboard and pieces on it
     * 2. scores of the players
     * 3. other help information
     */
    public void refreshOutput() {
        var size = this.configuration.getSize();
        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {
                    if (this.getCentralPlace().equals(new Place(col, row))) {
                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
                    var player = piece.getPlayer();
                    rowContent.add(String.format("%s%c%s",
                            player.getColor(),
                            piece.getLabel(),
                            Color.DEFAULT));
                }
            }
            contents.add(rowContent);
        }
        var xCoordinates = new ArrayList<String>();
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            xCoordinates.add(String.valueOf((char) ('a' + i)));
        }
        Collections.reverse(contents);

        // clear screen
        System.out.print("\u001b[2J");
        System.out.flush();

        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("### COMP3021 Programming Assignment 1 ###");
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Guide: to move a piece, input the coordinate of source and the destination.");
        System.out.println("For example: a1->b2 means to move the piece at 'a1' to 'b2'");
        if (this.numMoves < this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection()) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Notice: first " + this.configuration.getNumMovesProtection() + " moves are not allowed to" +
                    " capture pieces or win the game.");
        }
        System.out.println();
        System.out.println("Total Moves: " + this.numMoves);
        // print scores of players
        for (var player :
                this.configuration.getPlayers()) {
            System.out.printf("%s%s%s score: %d\n", player.getColor(), player.getName(), Color.DEFAULT,
                    player.getScore());
        }
        System.out.println();
        // print the gameboard
        var leftPadding = 8;
        var paddingSpaceBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        paddingSpaceBuilder.append(" ".repeat(leftPadding));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        var borderBuilder = new StringBuilder();
        borderBuilder.append("-".repeat(Math.max(0, contents.get(0).size() * 2 - 1)));
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        for (int row = contents.size() - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            System.out.printf("%" + (leftPadding - 1) + "d|%s|%d\n",
                    row + 1,
                    contents.get(row).parallelStream().map(Object::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(" ")),
                    row + 1);
        }
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                borderBuilder.toString());
        System.out.printf("%s%s\n",
                paddingSpaceBuilder.toString(),
                xCoordinates.parallelStream()
                        .collect(Collectors.joining(" ")));
        System.out.println();
    }

    /**
     * Get the piece in the place
     *
     * @param place the place of the piece
     * @return the piece
     */
    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(@NotNull Place place) {
        return this.board[place.x()][place.y()];
    }

    public @Nullable Piece getPiece(int x, int y) {
        return this.getPiece(new Place(x, y));
    }

    public Player getCurrentPlayer() {
        return currentPlayer != null ? currentPlayer : this.configuration.getPlayers()[0];
    }

    public Player[] getPlayers() {
        return configuration.getPlayers();
    }

    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    public Configuration getConfiguration() {
        return configuration;
    }

    public Place getCentralPlace() {
        return configuration.getCentralPlace();
    }

    @Override
    public Game clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Game) super.clone();
        cloned.configuration = this.configuration.clone();
        cloned.board = this.board.clone();
        for (int i = 0; i < this.configuration.getSize(); i++) {
            cloned.board[i] = this.board[i].clone();
            // no need to deep copy pieces
            if (this.configuration.getSize() >= 0)
                System.arraycopy(this.board[i], 0, cloned.board[i], 0, this.configuration.getSize());
        }
        cloned.currentPlayer = currentPlayer == null ? null : currentPlayer.clone();
        return cloned;
    }
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Move class represent a move made by a {@link Player}, moving a piece from one {@link Place} to another {@link Place}.
 */
public class Move implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Source place of the move.
     */
    private Place source;

    /**
     * Move destination
     */
    private Place destination;

    public Move(Place source, Place destination) {
        this.source = source;
        this.destination = destination;
    }

    public Move(int sourceX, int sourceY, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(new Place(sourceX, sourceY), new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    public Move(Place source, int destinationX, int destinationY) {
        this(source, new Place(destinationX, destinationY));
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public Place getSource() {
        return source;
    }

    public Place getDestination() {
        return destination;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Move move = (Move) o;
        return source.equals(move.source) &&
                destination.equals(move.destination);
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(source, destination);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Move.class.getSimpleName() + "[", "]")
                .add("source=" + source)
                .add("destination=" + destination)
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Move clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        var cloned = (Move) super.clone();
        cloned.source = this.source.clone();
        cloned.destination = this.destination.clone();
        return cloned;
    }

    /* Object methods end */

}
```

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.StringJoiner;

/**
 * A square (position, place) in the gameboard.
 * Represented by coordinates a 2-D coordinate system.
 * <p>
 * x and y coordinates of a place on gameboard are two fields of this class.
 */
public class Place implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * x coordinate
     */
    private final int x;

    /**
     * y coordinate
     */
    private final int y;

    public Place(int x, int y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }

    /* Getters start */
    public int x() {
        return x;
    }

    public int y() {
        return y;
    }
    /* Getters end */

    /* Object methods start */
    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;
        Place place = (Place) o;
        return x == place.x &&
                y == place.y;
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(x, y);
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return new StringJoiner(", ", Place.class.getSimpleName() + "(", ")")
                .add(String.valueOf(x))
                .add(String.valueOf(y))
                .toString();
    }

    @Override
    public Place clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        return (Place) super.clone();
    }
}
```

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}}; // Right, Left, Up, Down
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int x = source.x() + dx;
        int y = source.y() + dy;
        int boardSize = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
        
        // Check for normal moves (without capturing)
        while (x >= 0 && x < boardSize && y >= 0 && y < boardSize) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Move move = new Move(source, dest);
            if (game.getPiece(dest) == null) { // Empty square
                if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                    validMoves.add(move);
                }
                x += dx;
                y += dy;
                continue;
            }
            break; // Hit a piece, stop in this direction for normal moves
        }
        
        // Check for capture moves (must jump over exactly one piece)
        x = source.x() + dx;
        y = source.y() + dy;
        boolean foundPiece = false;
        
        while (x >= 0 && x < boardSize && y >= 0 && y < boardSize) {
            Place dest = new Place(x, y);
            Piece piece = game.getPiece(dest);
            
            if (!foundPiece) {
                if (piece != null) {
                    foundPiece = true;
                }
            } else {
                if (piece != null) {
                    // Check if it's an enemy piece
                    if (!piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayer())) {
                        Move move = new Move(source, dest);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            validMoves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
            x += dx;
            y += dy;
        }
    }
    
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    Piece movingPiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
    Piece destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    
    // If there's no piece at destination or the piece belongs to a different player, move is valid
    if (destinationPiece == null || !destinationPiece.getPlayer().equals(movingPiece.getPlayer())) {
        return true;
    }
    
    // Move is invalid if destination has a piece from the same player
    return false;
}
```

Explanation:
1. First, we get the piece that's being moved from the source location
2. Then we check what piece (if any) is at the destination location
3. The move is valid (returns true) if either:
   - There's no piece at the destination, OR
   - The piece at the destination belongs to a different player
4. The move is invalid (returns false) if there's a piece at the destination that belongs to the same player as the moving piece

This implementation follows the rule's description that "a piece should not go to a destination where there is another piece belonging to the same player."

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * The Game class
 */
public abstract class Game implements Cloneable {
    /**
     * Game configuration
     */
    protected Configuration configuration;

    /**
     * The gameboard, which is a 2-dimensional array of {@link Piece}, representing all the {@link Place} (squares) on
     * the board.
     * If there is a piece in some {@link Place} place(x,y), then {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]} will be the
     * piece object, otherwise null.
     * In other words, the board is a 2-D array with length equal to size of the board in both dimensions.
     */
    protected Piece[][] board;

     * Current player who is supposed to make a move.
     */
    protected Player currentPlayer;

     * The current number of moves made by two players
     */

        this.configuration = configuration;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    }

    /**
     * Start the game
     * Players will take turns according to the order in {@link Configuration#getPlayers()} to make a move until
     * a player wins.
     *
     * @return the winner
     */
    public abstract Player start();

    /**
     * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
     *
     * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
     * @param lastPiece the last piece that is moved by the player
     * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
     * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
     */
    public abstract Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove);

     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    public abstract void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move);

    public abstract @NotNull Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player);

        var contents = new ArrayList<List<String>>();
        for (int row = size - 1; row >= 0; row--) {
            var rowContent = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
                var piece = this.getPiece(col, row);
                if (piece == null) {

                        rowContent.add("x");
                    } else {
                        rowContent.add(".");
                    }
                } else {
```
